LESSON: MIRACLES OF PROPHETS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Pillars of Iman
Topic 3.3.2: Miracles of Prophets

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Miracles of Prophets. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is a miracle?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the miracles performed by the selected prophets to strengthen their iman (faith)
2. explain the lessons learnt from the miracles of the selected prophets
3. appreciate the miracles of the selected prophets to build their reliance on Allah

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MIRACLES OF PROPHETS
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Miracles of Prophets helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MIRACLES OF PROPHETS
Study Miracles of Prophets like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify the miracles performed by the selected prophets to strengthen their iman (faith)

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the miracles performed by the selected prophets to strengthen their iman (faith). You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the miracles performed by the selected prophets to strengthen their iman (faith).
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Miracles of Prophets” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the miracles performed by the selected prophets to strengthen their iman (faith). Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the lessons learnt from the miracles of the selected prophets

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the lessons learnt from the miracles of the selected prophets. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the lessons learnt from the miracles of the selected prophets.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Miracles of Prophets in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the lessons learnt from the miracles of the selected prophets. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the miracles of the selected prophets to build their reliance on Allah

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the miracles of the selected prophets to build their reliance on Allah. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the miracles of the selected prophets to build their reliance on Allah.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the miracles of the selected prophets to build their reliance on Allah. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Miracles of Prophets is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Miracles of Prophets” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify the miracles performed by the selected prophets to strengthen their iman (faith))

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Miracles of Prophets in your own words. (skill: explain the lessons learnt from the miracles of the selected prophets)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate the miracles of the selected prophets to build their reliance on Allah)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Miracles of Prophets to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the miracles performed by the selected prophets to strengthen their iman (faith).
3. Practise this skill: explain the lessons learnt from the miracles of the selected prophets.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the miracles of the selected prophets to build their reliance on Allah.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Miracles of Prophets from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Miracles of Prophets: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Miracles of Prophets?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is a miracle?
2. Why did prophets perform miracles?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Miracles of Prophets means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the miracles performed by the selected prophets to strengthen their iman (faith).
5. Be able to: explain the lessons learnt from the miracles of the selected prophets.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
